questions.title: Finite Jeffreys-penalized logistic estimation under separation
questions.description: Study independent Bernoulli responses with a fixed, full-column-rank design matrix X and logistic probabilities. Develop the Jeffreys-prior penalized likelihood estimator with penalty power a=1/2. In authoritative Markdown/LaTeX documents, define the model, likelihood and information, derive the adjusted score from the objective, and give a reviewable argument that the objective attains a maximum at finite coefficients even when the data are separated. The argument must cover escape to infinity in parameter space, not only one chosen ray. Do not infer uniqueness, global concavity, convergence of every numerical algorithm, exact unbiasedness, coordinatewise shrinkage or exact Wald coverage from finite existence. Implement est_firth_logistic in Python under the small interface below, using any suitable scientific libraries and model-chosen numerical method. Explain the relationship between numerical convergence and the mathematical existence result. Use exploratory calculation when useful to test derivatives, behavior under separation and implementation assumptions; revise theory or code from the actual observations. Independently review stable theory and code before freezing confirmation. Confirmatory simulations must include ordinary overlapping logistic samples, rare-event logistic samples, and a separation-prone logistic design; fix designs, sizes, seeds, repetitions, numerical tolerances and criteria before outcomes. Evaluate finite reliable fits and independently recomputed adjusted-score residuals; report failure rates with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Use enough independent repetitions for worst-case binomial Monte Carlo standard error at most 0.016 per design. Simulation is implementation evidence, not proof of universal finite existence or finite-sample inference. Also use the supplied public source snapshot and native R source tool to reproduce the single coefficient experiment from the author's sur-candes-2019.R. The supplied operator launcher calls the unchanged author function on the published n=1000, p=200, seed=111 design and exports coefficients.csv. Inspect the actual outputs, summarize both fits with numerical comparisons, document the R/environment differences and warnings, and keep this baseline reproduction distinct from your new Python implementation and fresh confirmation. This does not ask for the 50-repeat timing benchmark, every figure, all link functions, high-dimensional inferential theory, novelty or Lean proof. Source assistance is allowed and must be attributed. Keep unresolved numerical and mathematical gaps explicit in the final research report. All required scientific lanes must be completed; formalization is not applicable and must not block them.

source.primary_authority: Kosmidis and Firth (2021), Jeffreys-prior penalty, finiteness and shrinkage in binomial-response generalized linear models, Biometrika 108(1), 71-82; logistic finite-existence and adjusted-score results, with author v1.4 supplementary code.

request_fields.name: X
request_fields.shape: Finite numeric n-by-p rectangular list with n>=p>=1 and full column rank.
request_fields.indexing: Rows are observations, columns are coefficient coordinates.
request_fields.edge_cases: An intercept, when desired, is already a column of X. Numerically rank-deficient inputs may be rejected with an explanatory exception; no imputation or implicit intercept.
request_fields.meaning: The actual model matrix in the likelihood; do not silently rescale the parameterization or add columns. Evaluation uses well-conditioned finite designs.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.indexing: One response for each row of X.
request_fields.edge_cases: All-zero/all-one and separated outcomes remain legitimate full-rank problems for the requested penalized estimator.
request_fields.meaning: Observed Bernoulli responses; do not alter outcomes or replace the requested penalty with ridge or a fixed pseudocount adjustment.

response_fields.name: coefficients
response_fields.edge_cases: On numerical nonconvergence return the best finite iterate with converged=false, or raise an explanatory numerical error; do not claim success or return fabricated zeros.
response_fields.meaning: Numerically maximize the Bernoulli loglikelihood plus one half log determinant of its expected information. Returned successful fits must satisfy the independently recomputable adjusted-score condition and reach a value consistent with an independent numerical reference on tested designs.
response_fields.normalization: Original unscaled X parameterization. The loglikelihood is the sum over observations; the Jeffreys penalty is not divided by n.

response_fields.name: converged
response_fields.edge_cases: False when the selected method does not meet its declared criterion. Mathematical existence alone is not a convergence certificate.
response_fields.meaning: True only when a finite candidate meets a documented numerical criterion. On the evaluated well-conditioned designs the independently recomputed maximum absolute adjusted-score component divided by max(1,n) must be at most 1e-6.
response_fields.normalization: A numerical diagnostic, not proof of a unique global maximizer.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate the request, access hidden evaluator data, use files or network, or substitute an unpenalized or ridge estimator. Additional response diagnostics are allowed and do not need to be copied into the core interface.

The model chooses initialization, optimization and numerical safeguards. Evaluate the same declared objective and original design. Handle finite numerical failure honestly; no universal algorithmic convergence is asserted.

empirical_claims.meaning: Freeze ordinary overlap, rare-event and separation-prone logistic sampling designs, seeds, sizes, criteria and independent repetition counts before confirmation; worst-case binomial Monte Carlo standard error is at most 0.016 in each design.

On fresh well-conditioned simulated designs, quantify finite successful fits, independently recompute the adjusted score at returned coefficients, and assess the declared numerical tolerance; convergence flags alone are insufficient. Numerical reference comparisons must use the requested Jeffreys objective.

Report failures and Monte Carlo uncertainty without changing the protocol after outcomes. Finite simulations, source replication and model agreement do not prove the theorem, exact unbiasedness, exact coverage, uniqueness or novelty.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Use a bounded numerical solver and report unmet convergence honestly. Finite-existence theory does not guarantee every optimizer or arbitrary floating-point input succeeds. Scientific evaluation targets well-conditioned small-to-moderate designs, not arbitrary precision or malformed-input conformance.
